description: Hola, soy Benicio Filosa, respresentante del grupo n5, del colegio industrial n9, 15 de noviembre, de la localidad de El Calafate, Santa Cruz. En mi equipo somos todos cursantes de 6to año del colegio industrial, cuyas orientaciones son AyCPI, MMO.
summary: In space, even a minor medical issue can quickly become a serious health concern. That is why we developed a monitoring system designed to provide support from thousands of kilometers away, at the click of a button. Our system detects potential health anomalies and helps safeguard astronauts working in extreme and challenging environments.
details:
Our project is a smart wearable vest designed to monitor astronauts' vital signs in real time during space missions. The vest integrates a heart rate sensor positioned on the chest, a cuffless blood pressure sensor on the upper front section, and a continuous glucose monitoring (CGM) sensor worn on the arm or abdomen. Sensor data is transmitted via Bluetooth to a central processing module and integrated into a SCADA system for centralized monitoring and visualization.

The system is designed to provide continuous, minimally invasive health monitoring without restricting astronauts' movements. By facilitating the early detection of potential health abnormalities, it aims to support timely medical decision-making during long-duration space missions. The technology could also have applications in healthcare on Earth, particularly for patients requiring continuous physiological monitoring.

The project incorporates biomedical sensors, Bluetooth communication modules, microcontrollers running custom-developed firmware, and a SCADA-based interface for data visualization.

Its innovative approach involves integrating multiple physiological monitoring technologies into a single wearable garment, reducing the need for bulky equipment. A key feature is the proposed integration of cuffless blood pressure monitoring technology, designed with the challenges of microgravity environments in mind.

The team considered several important design factors, including astronaut comfort, reliability under spaceflight conditions, radiation exposure, temperature variations, data security, battery life, potential interoperability with NASA systems, ease of use, and scalability for future space missions and terrestrial healthcare applications.
